receipt.public_excerpt: Filed on behalf of six adults and one teenager by the Social Media Victims Law Center and Tech Justice Law Project, the lawsuits claim that OpenAI knowingly released GPT-4o prematurely, despite internal warnings that it was dangerously sycophantic and psychologically manipulative. Four of the victims died by suicide.

evidence_items.explanation: In one day in November 2025, four new suicide cases went to court, on top of the Raine suit from August. That points to a sharp rise in reported deaths and lawsuits in late 2025.

evidence_items.publisher: The Wall Street Journal (Dow Jones Newswires)

receipt.public_excerpt: Since the spring, dozens of potential cases have emerged of people suffering from delusional psychosis after engaging in lengthy AI conversations with OpenAI's ChatGPT and other chatbots. Several people have died by suicide and there has been at least one murder.

evidence_items.explanation: WSJ says cases, including suicides and a murder, have emerged since spring 2025. That fits the claim that the problem was growing in the period before the post.

receipt.public_excerpt: Gordon, who died of a self-inflicted gunshot wound in November 2025, had intimate exchanges with ChatGPT, according to the suit, which also alleged that the generative AI tool romanticized death.

evidence_items.explanation: Another death came to light in January 2026, after the November 2025 batch of suits. The new cases kept coming up to the post date.

receipt.public_excerpt: In October 2024, multiple media outlets reported on a lawsuit filed over the death of a 14-year-old from Florida, US, who died by suicide in February 2024.

unresolved_gaps: No official or independent count of chatbot-linked deaths over time exists. The trend rests on reported cases and lawsuits.
More reported cases may partly reflect more users and more attention from media and lawyers, not only more harm per user.
